title: Map enterprise planning and decision platforms
accept: Distinguish vendor claims from implementation evidence for DIOS, o9, Maestro, Blue Yonder, SAP, Siemens, Oracle and Foundry. Record integration, scenarios and undisclosed limits.

title: Compare optimizers and modeling languages
accept: Compare AIMMS, Gurobi, Xpress, CPLEX, OR-Tools, Timefold, Hexaly, Pyomo, JuMP, MiniZinc and OptaPlanner by abstraction, license and capabilities.

title: Map optimization science and computational limits
accept: Cover every method in section 4.2 with assumptions, complexity, memory, guarantees and integration priority. Include a relationship diagram.

title: Review prior art, publications and patent claims
accept: Compare component reuse, IR lowering and algorithm selection with published precedents. Record identifiers, overlap and unknowns.

title: Model pilot economics and select verticals
accept: Score manufacturing against other verticals. Expose cost inputs, delivery assumptions and a falsifiable buyer hypothesis.

title: Validate demand and pilot data with a design partner
accept: Obtain authorized anonymized data, planner baseline, signed metric definitions and buying feedback. Keep customer records outside git.

title: Qualify native adapters and redistribution
accept: Run pinned OR-Tools and HiGHS fixtures on Windows and Linux. Inventory native components, ABI, notices and transitive licenses. Assess SCIP, Math.NET and ML.NET separately.

title: Approve the phase-zero evidence dossier
accept: Review source gaps, solver claims and product scope. Record go, revise or stop before releasing production software.

title: Publish system boundaries and architecture decisions
accept: Diagram component ownership, compare deployment alternatives, describe storage and UI decisions and extraction triggers.

title: Establish contributor intake and coordination
accept: Publish English and Arabic entry points, claim protocol, isolated worktrees, PR checklist and contract-owner policy.

title: Build cross-platform validation pipeline
accept: Run portable research checks on Linux and Windows. Surface reproducible commands and failures on pull requests.

title: Design tenant threat model and trust boundaries
accept: Review imports, plugins, cache isolation, identity, evidence export and system-of-record writes. Define defensive tests.

title: Version API, schema and extension contracts
accept: Publish compatibility policy with a backward-compatible extension, breaking migration example and rejection fixtures.

title: Define revisioned entity and hyperedge graph
accept: Represent all named EDG concepts and interval, capacity and provenance relationships. Show multi-variable constraint scopes.

title: Index dependencies and impact across revisions
accept: Compare incremental reachability to complete traversal including deleted and newly introduced edges and global objectives.

title: Implement typed UDIR and source spans
accept: Encode domains, rational literals, units, currencies, time basis, uncertainty, requirements and semantic versions. Round-trip fixtures.

title: Validate dimensions, calendars and currency conversion
accept: Reject implicit currency conversion, inconsistent time bases and overflow. Accept an explicit versioned rate and exact scale.

title: Specify DML grammar, AST and diagnostics
accept: Parse valid and invalid examples with spans and stable error codes. Define grammar extension rules for scenarios and triggers.

title: Build bounded declarative parser and binder
accept: Reject unknown symbols, cycles in derived expressions, excessive input and arbitrary executable constructs.

title: Implement semantic analysis and normalization
accept: Normalize equivalent exact expressions, retain provenance and compare finite feasible sets before and after transformation.

title: Implement capability-checked solver lowering
accept: Reject unsupported requirements and rounding. Map native indices to source constraints and distinguish exact from approximate transformations.

title: Expose typed C# modeling SDK
accept: Construct a production and workforce model with no strings for unit arithmetic. Compare normalized IR with DML equivalents.

title: Deliver JSON Schema and versioned model import
accept: Validate domain and schema separately. Reject unknown mandatory semantics, malformed bounds and duplicate keys.

title: Implement immutable model registry and provenance
accept: Persist tenant-scoped model revisions, source hashes and snapshots. Resolve old revisions after schema migration.

title: Implement safe presolve and transformation ledger
accept: Check tautologies, duplicates, unused variables and empty domains; preserve reconstruction metadata and counterexamples.

title: Define solver capability and result contracts
accept: Separate mathematical status, termination reason, incumbent, bounds, tolerances, trust source and resource use.

title: Integrate integer scheduling adapter
accept: Solve a precedence and no-overlap fixture using CP-SAT; preserve domain bounds, horizon semantics and native status.

title: Integrate LP and MILP adapter
accept: Solve and independently check LP and integer fixtures via HiGHS; handle native failures and unsupported certificates.

title: Implement independent feasibility and cost checker
accept: Check original-model assignments, integrality, intervals, capacities and every objective without calling the lowering layer.

title: Validate bounds and classify evidence strength
accept: Reject wrong-direction and stale bounds. Reproduce a primal/dual or enumeration proof; distinguish solver attestation.

title: Implement capability-first solver planning
accept: Filter by semantics then choose an eligible algorithm using features, budget and a documented tie-break; explain rejections.

title: Govern worker CPU, memory, queues and deadlines
accept: Exercise quotas with competing tenants, solver subprocess crashes, cancellation and timeouts without leaking leases.

title: Implement budgeted solver portfolio
accept: Charge cumulative core-seconds, cap concurrent native threads and compare equal-budget single solver runs.

title: Enable compatible hints and solver switching
accept: Map hints to the current revision, discard invalid bounds and stop workers on budget expiry, retaining best verified incumbent.

title: Persist evidence, lineage and audit reports
accept: Export input hash, solver version, termination, tolerances, verifier, hardware, timestamps and reproducible invocation.

title: Implement decision state machine and approval policies
accept: Test each allowed and forbidden transition; bind sensitive approvals to verified immutable revisions with separation of duties.

title: Expose REST API and idempotent job worker
accept: Submit, poll, cancel and replay an authenticated, budgeted job using the planner and a qualified adapter. Reject idempotency conflicts and publish verified evidence under a fenced lease.

title: Run exhaustive separability and reuse experiment
accept: Compare full enumeration with component reuse after a local change, then test shared capacities, coupled objectives and stale cache inputs.

title: Detect exact components and certify separability
accept: Check complete constraint and objective scopes, including implicit global resources; reconstruct a verified solution from independent components.

title: Produce canonical fingerprints and reuse permissions
accept: Separate structure, data, constraints, objectives and solver config; exercise deletion, reordered input, tenant and compiler version.

title: Validate cache entries and prevent stale bound reuse
accept: Replay changed units, objectives, adapter versions and data. Cache misses or revalidation must preserve evidence strength.

title: Implement bounded repair and full-solve fallback
accept: Treat fixed-boundary solutions as feasible unless certified. Re-expand on failed verification, crossing constraints or insufficient quality.

title: Evaluate separators, SCCs and coordinated decomposition
accept: Contrast SCCs with primal incidence components. Test Benders or pricing only for structures satisfying documented assumptions.

title: Build reproducible benchmark harness and corpus
accept: Record seed, dataset license, hardware, warm/cold setup, wall time, core seconds, peak RSS, gap and timeout censoring.

title: Evaluate incremental and portfolio hypotheses
accept: Compare cold full, hinted full, component reuse and repair under matched budgets; publish failures, confidence intervals and ablations.

title: Evaluate learned selection against deterministic policy
accept: Hold out instance families; include feature extraction overhead and single-best baseline. Disable ML unless acceptance threshold holds.

title: Maintain innovation register and stop decisions
accept: Record prior art, proof assumptions, benchmark results, failure regions and novelty status per hypothesis.

title: Specify manufacturing datasets and optimization model
accept: Define machine calendars, materials, precedence, release dates, due dates and cost units. Hand-check at least one optimum.

title: Implement deterministic dispatch baseline
accept: Provide earliest-due-date baseline with stable tie-break and explicit failure for infeasible material or calendar assignments.

title: Implement finite-capacity production scheduling
accept: Output a checkable schedule with finite materials, machines, deadlines and weighted tardiness. Explain any infeasible fixture.

title: Deliver outage and demand-change scenarios
accept: Branch immutable inputs for machine downtime and changed demand. Compare lateness, cost and stability using the same units.

title: Validate pilot against planner historical schedule
accept: Replay an agreed horizon, expose all exclusions and measure verified outcomes against planner and dispatch baselines.

title: Specify independent workforce coverage model
accept: Encode shifts, skills and capacity with cost and coverage, using no manufacturing dependencies.

title: Demonstrate core reuse across sectors
accept: Run workforce fixtures including infeasible coverage. Identify reused contracts and domain-specific code by dependency checks.

title: Define connector SDK and mapping manifests
accept: Specify field type, unit, provenance, mapping version, cursor, retries, reconciliation and credentials by reference.

title: Implement CSV and JSON snapshot import
accept: Test encoding, decimal conventions, errors per row, repeat ingestion and reversed input order.

title: Implement REST ingestion and authenticated webhooks
accept: Test duplicate delivery, ordering gaps, replay, pagination and retry ceilings using fake peers.

title: Implement incremental sync, recovery and health
accept: Persist cursor atomically with writes, recover after process failure, quarantine invalid data and report freshness.

title: Deliver optional WOW ERP connector
accept: Provide sandbox contract fixtures, mapped fields and opt-in scopes. Core tests must pass with the adapter absent.

title: Qualify SAP, Oracle and Dynamics adapters
accept: For each vendor pin the supported API, mapping and replay contract; require authorized sandbox evidence before enabling.

title: Qualify Odoo, ERPNext and custom ERP adapters
accept: Exercise independent versioned field mappings and cursor reconciliation per platform; publish adapter capability sheets.

title: Add SQL, Excel and event-stream adapters
accept: Test read-only queries, workbook data types, offsets and replay semantics. Reject invalid units and partial snapshots.

title: Qualify CRM, MES, WMS and IoT feeds
accept: Validate freshness, event IDs, clock skew and schema revisions per source with recorded non-customer fixtures.

title: Implement immutable scenario comparison
accept: Compare baseline and scenario on matched units and horizon, distinguishing changed inputs from output differences.

title: Explain decisions, alternatives and conflicts
accept: Report objective decomposition, binding constraints and a forced alternative re-solve. Distinguish IIS from minimum repair.

title: Implement LP sensitivity and relaxation analysis
accept: Restrict dual prices to valid LP assumptions and ranges. Verify discrete alternatives by re-solving.

title: Add discrete-event and Monte Carlo simulation
accept: Validate queue dynamics on a deterministic fixture and reject biased causal claims from simulated trials.

title: Model forecast uncertainty and risk
accept: Backtest prediction intervals, robust sets and stochastic plans with held-out scenarios; report coverage and downside metrics.

title: Add verified advisory recommendations and optional MCP
accept: Recommendations reference verified evidence. Test read-only scoped MCP access and operation without an LLM or paid service.

title: Ship cross-platform professional CLI
accept: Coordinate local commands over the application ports, structured output, installation and independent offline execution. Remote transport is qualified separately in RT05.

title: Qualify Microsoft Blazor desktop delivery
accept: Test installable window, offline startup, keyboard navigation, RTL and packaging on Windows and Linux. Document host ownership.

title: Build visual modeling studio and graph explorer
accept: Round-trip typed edits and compare hyperedges and dependency impact across two graph revisions with source provenance.

title: Build scheduling and scenario workspace
accept: Show resource usage, timeline, alternatives and changed constraints. Test keyboard and screen-reader flows.

title: Build evidence viewer and benchmark dashboard
accept: Display solver and verifier statuses separately, export reproducible evidence, surface unknown gaps and censored runs.

title: Build administration and developer portals
accept: Exercise tenant roles, connector health, schemas, SDK examples and audit search using a least-privilege account.

title: Implement tenant-aware identity and authorization
accept: Authenticate through OIDC, bind jobs to tenant, reject cross-tenant lookups and audit denied access without secrets.

title: Persist models and jobs with EF Core
accept: Exercise PostgreSQL migrations, tenant keys, concurrent revision writes and backup restore. Document SQL Server portability differences.

title: Implement outbox, scheduling and notifications
accept: Crash between commit and publish, replay duplicate events and show a single logical notification with bounded retries.

title: Implement human approvals and gated external execution
accept: Require authorized approval for a verified revision and single logical execution; stale approvals and ambiguous side effects fail closed.

title: Add telemetry, audit retention and operations tools
accept: Trace model-to-run without exposing customer input; verify retention, redaction, restore drills and per-tenant cost attribution.

title: Package self-hosted Docker and SaaS profiles
accept: Smoke-test air-gapped install and hosted configuration, upgrade/rollback with data compatibility and secret rotation.

title: Isolate extension code and native workers
accept: Run plugins out of process with explicit permissions; test resource limits, process expiry and fail-closed startup.

title: Implement scale-out queue and resource fairness
accept: Exercise competing tenants, duplicate workers, lease expiry and overload; publish throughput and fairness by workload.

title: Add compiler property and differential tests
accept: Generate bounded models and compare original, normalized and lowered feasible assignments, objectives and diagnostic spans.

title: Run integration, accessibility and isolation tests
accept: Review independent local, embedded, desktop, CLI and enterprise suites. Each release consumes only its applicable evidence.

title: Publish release evidence and licensing inventory
accept: Produce checksums, dependency inventory, notices, supported OS matrix, operator guide and reproducible release checklist.

title: Decide MVP, enterprise and scale release gates
accept: Publish six independent release decisions with explicit evidence, exclusions and sign-off. Gate criteria are versioned separately from gate execution.

title: Evaluate expansion across proposed sectors
accept: Score inventory, logistics, transport, retail, health, finance, cash flow, energy, construction, projects, agriculture, telecom, cloud and data centers by data availability, risk and value before opening delivery epics.

title: Audit scope traceability and reconcile the engineering plan
accept: Publish a checked traceability baseline, original design archive, verified dependency repairs and open gaps.

title: Application shell
accept: Resize two panes, reopen a saved layout and switch tabs by keyboard while the selected revision remains stable.

title: Workspace manager
accept: Create a local workspace, back it up, restore into another directory and compare revision and evidence digests.

title: Overview dashboard
accept: Exercise an empty workspace and one with two runs. Follow a recent decision to its exact revision.

title: Visual model designer
accept: Build the Batch example by pointer and keyboard, then compare normalized output with the DSL fixture.

title: Enterprise decision graph explorer
accept: Select a three-variable constraint, filter an edge and compare before/after reachability against the unfiltered graph queries.

title: Decision DSL editor
accept: Edit a symbol in Batch, navigate to its exact diagnostic, repair the edit and compare formatted and original typed trees.

title: Constraint editor
accept: Save an equivalent capacity expression in two units and compare normalized quantities and bound inclusivity.

title: Objective editor
accept: Reverse one goal direction, adjust a weight and compare a known assignment against the displayed objective vector.

title: Mathematical model inspector
accept: Follow one normalized row across all views back to its original span and inspect the reconstruction rule.

title: Solver configuration
accept: Select auto on a finite interval model, explain eligibility and round-trip its budget through the planner.

title: Optimization monitor
accept: Replay events with an incumbent and absent bound. Show measured values and preserve the verified incumbent after cancellation.

title: Algorithm execution visualizer
accept: Compare a disconnected edit and a new coupling edge. Link each reuse or fallback to its recorded evidence.

title: Scenario comparison studio
accept: Compare two frozen revisions, show changed inputs and report comparable cost deltas with units.

title: Simulation studio
accept: Replay identical seeds and compare quantiles, sample counts and event traces against recorded simulation output.

title: Production scheduling studio
accept: Select an operation before and after an outage, confirm its half-open interval and expose its machine and original-model checks.

title: Resource allocation visualizer
accept: Reconcile occupied machine minutes with capacity in the same frozen horizon and drill into each contributing operation.

title: Decision evidence viewer
accept: Open a timed-out run with verified incumbent and inspect source rows, objective and absent certificate separately.

title: Explainability studio
accept: Compare a forced alternative to the baseline using identical input and budget and trace any claim to its evidence.

title: Performance and benchmark studio
accept: Display paired samples, hardware, seeds, peak memory and failed trials from a benchmark manifest.

title: Integration mapping designer
accept: Map a source quantity to an engine field, preview normalized values and trace rejected rows to source fields.

title: Administration and developer portal
accept: Use two tenant accounts to check a read-only role, an administrative operation and versioned SDK examples in Blazor.

title: Command palette and productivity
accept: Invoke a registered command by name and shortcut with the same permission and workspace context.

title: Settings and diagnostics
accept: Change theme and language, restart and inspect the effective configuration and redacted health report.

title: Command host and registration
accept: Launch help and version from a clean directory without database, network or native solver initialization.

title: Terminal presentation
accept: Snapshot a wide and narrow TTY and redirected output. Record exactly which events generated each progress line.

title: Workspace command family
accept: Initialize a temporary workspace, reopen it by path and compare exported revision identity after a second process reads it.

title: Model command family
accept: Import two revisions, compile a supported model and compare its inspected source mappings with the exported model.

title: Optimization command family
accept: Run a factory fixture locally, verify a candidate, cancel a second run and confirm dry-run starts no solver process.

title: Graph command family
accept: Change one coupling and compare exported impact membership with a full traversal of both revisions.

title: Scenario and simulation commands
accept: Freeze a baseline, create a delta, compare results and replay a seeded simulation from its manifest.

title: Decision and evidence commands
accept: Verify an exported solution against the original model in a fresh workspace and compare the recorded objective.

title: Solver and benchmark commands
accept: Run paired instances with a fixed budget, enumerate adapter versions and retain failures in the report.

title: Diagnostics commands
accept: Run doctor without a workspace and against an unreadable local path. Check actionable diagnostics and redacted configuration.

title: Machine output and automation
accept: Pipe JSON to a parser while reading progress on stderr, parse quoted CSV and cancel a child process without leaving a worker.

title: CLI packaging and installation
accept: Install from a local feed on clean Windows and Linux, run inside a container and solve using only packaged dependencies.

title: Shared visual tokens
accept: Map dark reference colors and dimensions to named tokens. Render the same states in all themes and check contrast on text and focus rings.

title: Accessible component gallery
accept: Traverse a modal and editable table using keyboard alone. Confirm accessible names, focus restoration and distinct live announcements.

title: Desktop layouts and localization
accept: Switch language at runtime, move the window between monitors and verify logical focus order and usable split views at two scale factors.

title: Graph and chart primitives
accept: Render a hyperedge, select it with the keyboard and compare its incident IDs to the accessible table. Link chart points to the stored run events.

title: Offline local runtime
accept: Disable network, create and reopen a workspace, persist a frozen revision and replay an export with the same evidence identity.

title: Enterprise host conformance
accept: Run two tenants using identical client-generated model IDs and prove isolated reads, job cancellation and audit trails.

title: Headless execution conformance
accept: Unset display, block outbound network, execute a published CLI fixture and verify exit status and evidence digest.

title: Embedded SDK distribution
accept: Build a fresh consumer from a local package feed, evaluate Batch and verify against the same original-model checker without server or UI.

title: Hybrid routing and credentials
accept: Keep local execution usable when the server is down. Reconnect and correlate a remote result with its exact submitted revision.

title: Numerical invariants and reproducibility
accept: Enumerate small exact models and test equivalent unit scalings, boundary residuals and overflowing coefficients; compare repeat runs under a pinned profile.

title: Multi-objective solving semantics
accept: Compare a tiny two-objective model against an enumerated nondominated set. Establish each higher-priority bound before declaring lexicographic optimality.

title: Robust and stochastic models
accept: Check a two-stage example against enumerated scenarios and verify that first-stage choices agree on identical information sets.

title: Online reoptimization study
accept: Replay timestamped disruptions under an equal budget and compare decisions to cold full solves on identical observed prefixes.

title: Algorithm and solver extension registry
accept: Load two versioned manifests, reject a mismatched capability and survive adapter process failure without losing verified evidence.

title: Optional provider contracts
accept: Run core conformance with no provider installed and inspect provider-specific diagnostics for unsupported operations.

title: Validated language-model proposals
accept: Submit an ambiguous request, review missing fields, validate generated DML and verify each explanatory claim against an evidence reference.

title: Forecast qualification
accept: Use chronological holdouts and report interval coverage, error, drift and failure rates against a seasonal baseline.

title: Five-strategy comparative study
accept: Freeze holdout families, observed data and budget. Publish positive, negative and missing outcomes across profit, cost, utilization, feasibility, violations, gaps, latency, CPU, memory, training, inference, disruption adaptation, explanation, reproducibility and robustness.

title: Local and SDK contract suite
accept: Run the same factory and workforce fixtures via offline and package consumers; compare source-domain checks, identity and objective.

title: Desktop visual and accessibility qualification
accept: Capture actual windows at reference logical size and 3x scale; store fonts, OS, host, fixture, tolerance calibration and per-region diff.

title: Command-line release conformance
accept: Exercise an actual installed binary on both platforms with a TTY, redirected streams and a blocked network.

title: Enterprise reliability qualification
accept: Stress two concurrent tenants and record queue fairness, peak memory, leaked workers and verified terminal outcomes under worker restart.

title: Compiler and solver robustness suite
accept: Compare generated bounded source models with exact enumeration after normalization and independent verification; persist minimized seeds and rejection reasons.

title: Secure data movement and retention
accept: Exercise authorized redacted export, invalid archive sizes and expired retention while preserving the audit record and reference integrity.

title: Release provenance and secure updates
accept: Generate an SBOM per RID, verify signatures offline and exercise rollback after interrupted installation.

title: Restore and disaster recovery
accept: Restore a tenant snapshot into a fresh instance, reconcile outbox/lease state and measure recovery time and lost writes.

title: Factory vertical slice and evidence
accept: Replay the same authorized fixture, change one machine availability, run both incremental and full paths, and export verifiable evidence for each OS and each client.

title: Independent workforce end-to-end slice
accept: Use a workforce domain assembly with no manufacturing dependency. Replay availability change and verify coverage and cost against a small independent oracle.

title: Research prototype gate
accept: Repeat a finite experiment on a clean host and publish the falsification case with its raw evidence.

title: MVP gate
accept: Replay factory import through both installed clients, verify outage and full comparison, and attach Windows/Linux evidence for the shipping subset.

title: Production release gate
accept: Run offline install, upgrade, restore and rollback on supported hosts, and verify no loss of accepted revisions.

title: Enterprise release gate
accept: Demonstrate tenant isolation, failover and human approval on a clean tenant pair with audit export.

title: Multi-sector platform gate
accept: Install both verticals against the same core build and compare semantic verification across their own baselines.

title: Scale release gate
accept: Publish reproducible saturation curves with quotas, workload mix, hardware, latency distributions and recovery results.

title: Versioned field and contract dictionary
accept: Trace each pilot field through every applicable layer and exercise one valid and one invalid representation in contract tests.

title: Studio module specification and design review
accept: Check each module against the visual source and review its distinct navigation, loading, invalid input, unavailable data, keyboard path and recovery before feature implementation.

title: Editable architecture and subsystem diagrams
accept: Render editable sources, verify each edge against the documented contract, and associate requirements, issue IDs and explicit failure/recovery paths.

title: Product and delivery specifications
accept: Trace an operator journey and SDK consumer from the PRD to versioned fields, acceptance tests and release-specific evidence.

title: Research hypothesis dossiers
accept: Review H1–H5 individually with counterexamples and before/after flows. Mark unmeasured results and record the rejection rule before running experiments.

title: Studio design system and desktop experience
accept: Review gallery, module contracts, host qualification and applicable OS evidence before accepting a desktop release.

title: Runtime modes and distribution contracts
accept: Publish a mode-by-mode conformance report and verify consistent contracts across all five modes.

title: Product specifications and editable engineering diagrams
accept: Resolve each mandated specification and diagram to reviewed source, owning requirement and test oracle.

title: Numerical, extension and research qualification
accept: Distinguish mathematical proof, measured experiment and capability limitation for each research item.

title: Security and recovery controls
accept: Review verified controls and qualification evidence independently for each release tier.

title: Cross-product vertical slice acceptance
accept: Accept each sector only after a complete replay through the published clients and original-model verification.

title: Inventory feasibility and model study
accept: Specify SKU stock and reorder lots with orders per period. On stock-movement ledger, compare holding plus shortage cost against seasonal reorder point subject to inventory balance, lead time and service. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Supply chain feasibility and model study
accept: Specify plants, suppliers and arcs with source and flow quantities. On dated purchase and shipment snapshots, compare landed cost against fixed sourcing proportions subject to lead time, capacity and material conservation. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Logistics feasibility and model study
accept: Specify depots, parcels and dispatch slots with parcel-to-route assignment. On anonymized dispatch manifests, compare late deliveries and distance against first-fit dispatch subject to cutoffs, vehicle capacities and windows. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Transportation feasibility and model study
accept: Specify vehicles, trips and stations with trip assignment and departure. On licensed timetable and travel-time matrix, compare cancelled trips and operating cost against published timetable subject to headway, turnaround and availability. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Retail feasibility and model study
accept: Specify stores, assortments and shelves with SKU allocation per store. On anonymized store-week demand, compare margin after shrinkage against historical replenishment subject to shelf space, stock and minimum assortment. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Healthcare feasibility and model study
accept: Specify clinics, rooms and visit slots with elective appointment assignment. On synthetic appointments with no patient identifiers, compare wait and overtime against manual appointment list subject to capacity, credentials and priority rules. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Finance feasibility and model study
accept: Specify instruments, exposures and limits with bounded allocation. On licensed historical prices and synthetic portfolios, compare scenario risk-adjusted return against fixed allocation policy subject to portfolio exposure and liquidity limits. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Cash flow feasibility and model study
accept: Specify accounts, obligations and receipts with cash transfers by date. On synthetic dated obligations, compare interest and shortfall against treasury calendar policy subject to minimum balance, currency and settlement. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Energy feasibility and model study
accept: Specify generators, meters and periods with unit dispatch. On public hourly load with licensed generator data, compare generation cost and deficit against dispatch merit order subject to ramp, capacity and reserve. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Construction feasibility and model study
accept: Specify sites, crews, trades and lifts with work package start and crew assignment. On synthetic site schedule and calendars, compare delay and idle cost against critical path with leveling subject to precedence, safety windows and crane capacity. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Project management feasibility and model study
accept: Specify tasks, skills and teams with task start and assignment. On licensed project scheduling instances, compare late milestones and staffing cost against priority-list scheduling subject to precedence, milestones and skill pools. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Agriculture feasibility and model study
accept: Specify plots, crops and irrigation slots with planting and water allocation. On regional weather and synthetic farm inventory, compare yield margin and water use against fixed crop calendar subject to soil, rotation, water and seasonal bounds. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Telecommunications feasibility and model study
accept: Specify links, traffic classes and capacity with traffic routing and capacity reservation. On synthetic network and held-out traffic demand, compare congestion and unserved demand against shortest feasible path subject to flow conservation, link limits and latency. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Cloud resources feasibility and model study
accept: Specify instances, jobs and quotas with instance placement and sizing. On synthetic job arrival traces, compare compute cost and deadline misses against first-fit decreasing subject to memory, cores and regional quotas. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.

title: Data centers feasibility and model study
accept: Specify racks, servers and power zones with placement and power scheduling. On synthetic rack inventory and power traces, compare energy plus unmet service against static rack assignment subject to thermal envelope, power caps and redundancy. Record units, solver capabilities, input rights, integration fields, uncertainty and rejection thresholds before an experiment.
